method: Known victims listed individually in the existing catalog each contribute one. Sourced group totals override that lower bound, include named victims within the total, and are not added to them. Confirmed minimums omit unverified additional casualties. Unlocated scenes stay off the heatmap.

entries.title: Nope
entries.basis: The screenplay stages 40 audience members initially, then specifies forty people swept into the creature and 40 park attendees inside it. The released newscast counts 40 guests and employees together. Use the combined count and avoid adding performers or employees to it. The newscast reports missing persons, with the fate of the swallowed group implied by the film. The park is the attack origin. The precise location where the group dies inside the airborne creature is uncertain.

evidence.reference: Peele screenplay pp. 57–58, 62 and 71, lines 2171, 2333–2352 and 2635–2643

evidence.quote: those 40 guests and employees of a local Western theme park are still unknown

entries.title: L.A. Confidential
entries.basis: Dudley Smith gives six victims at the police briefing for the Nite Owl massacre and names Dick Stensland as one of them.

evidence.quote: Six victims. One of them, one of our own -- Dick Stensland.

entries.title: The Terminator
entries.basis: The sequel names the station attacked in 1984 and gives the officer death toll. This evidence establishes the count and does not establish geographic placement.

evidence.reference: Terminator 2 shooting screenplay p. 43, scenes 55–56, lines 1171–1190
evidence.quote: He killed seventeen police officers that night.

evidence.reference: Released-film interview clip starts at 00:44:46. Mossberg states count at 00:08 in clip.
evidence.quote: He killed 17 police officers that night

entries.title: Heat
entries.basis: Hanna's crime-scene account identifies two killed guards and a third killed as a witness.

evidence.quote: after they killed two guards... ...they didn't hesitate. Popped guard number three

entries.title: Reservoir Dogs
entries.basis: Mr. Blonde, Officer Marvin Nash, Joe Cabot and Nice Guy Eddie are confirmed killed in the warehouse. The script has White fire with his gun against Orange's head and then be struck by police fire, but does not explicitly state either death. AFI describes the released ending as police shooting White before he fires, so Orange and White are excluded from the confirmed minimum. The screenplay uses Jeffrey Andrews for the captive officer. AFI identifies the released-film character as Marvin Nash.

evidence.quote: police burst in and shoot him before he pulls the trigger

entries.title: Assault on Precinct 13
entries.basis: Dialogue counts five officers, Julie and one prisoner after the initial attacks. AFI confirms Julie is discovered dead inside the station and places the prison transport casualties at the station exit. Wells dies after driving away to a phone booth. The movie also depicts attacker fatalities and gives a rough dialogue estimate, so seven is a conservative lower bound based on the explicit defender-side count.

evidence.quote: They gunned down five police officers, a secretary, one prisoner!

entries.title: The Rocketeer
entries.basis: Conservative minimum: seven separately portrayed gunfire casualties in the released Observatory shootout, plus the commando dragged over the ledge, whose death is explicit in scene 120. The screenplay’s twenty attackers are not treated as twenty deaths. Airship and Hollywoodland-sign deaths are excluded from the Observatory ground count.

evidence.reference: Shootout excerpt, 00:15–00:21, 00:24–00:30, 00:43–00:44 and 00:50–00:52; reviewed frame by frame.
Scenes 118–122: printed pp. 103–106 / PDF pages 118–121. Scene 120 identifies the fallen commando as dead; twenty is the attacker count, not a death tally.

entries.title: The Terminator
entries.basis: Two Observatory punks: the leader played by Bill Paxton and the knife-wielding punk played by Brian Thompson. Both actors explicitly recall being killed. The third punk gives up his clothes; no death is established.

evidence.reference: Bill Paxton: Punk Leader and Brian Thompson: Punk, first-person recollections published 31 January 2024.

entries.title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
entries.basis: Rick recounts two intruders killed by his friend and dog, followed by the third intruder killed by Rick. These are fictional events in the film; surviving residents, guests and the dog are not victims.

evidence.reference: Final Rick/Jay conversation after the attack: two intruders killed by Cliff and Brandy, plus the third killed by Rick.
